definition: In rem is Latin for “against the thing,” and indicates that a legal concept concerns things rather than people. A lawsuit in rem is a lawsuit against a thing, rather than against a person, which resolves rights or interests related to that thing.  For example: in United States v. 422 Casks of Wine the United States initiated a lawsuit against 422 casks of wine, claiming that it had the right to seize the casks because they had been deliberately mislabeled as sherry to avoid taxes.
